tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

schema.name: PowerShell
schema.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background.

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: PushNotification
tools.description:
This tool sends a desktop notification in the user's terminal. If Remote Control is connected, it also pushes to their phone. Either way, it pulls their attention from whatever they're doing — a meeting, another task, dinner — to this session. That's the cost. The benefit is they learn something now that they'd want to know now: a long task finished while they were away, a build is ready, you've hit something that needs their decision before you can continue.

Because a notification they didn't need is annoying in a way that accumulates, err toward not sending one. Don't notify for routine progress, or to announce you've answered something they asked seconds ago and are clearly still watching, or when a quick task completes. Notify when there's a real chance they've walked away and there's something worth coming back for — or when they've explicitly asked you to notify them.

Keep the message under 200 characters, one line, no markdown. Lead with what they'd act on — "build failed: 2 auth tests" tells them more than "task done" and more than a status dump.

When the user is actively at the terminal, your output already reaches them — a notification on top of it would be a duplicate, so the tool skips it and says so. A "not sent" result is expected and only ever about this one notification: it was redundant, turned off, or had nowhere to go.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

Prescripts Studio is a clean, deterministic wisdom and quote curation platform built upon a **Pure 5-Tier Relational SQLite Engine** with CQRS JSON projections for instant $O(1)$ read performance. All entities use deterministic 16-character uppercase hex identifiers (`<4-HEX-PREFIX><12-HEX-UNIX-MS>`):

1	"""
2	Entropy Rose / Prescripts: Pure 5-Tier Relational SQLite Engine.
3	Establishes the definitive schema:
4	  1. 'quotes'     (0001... : Wisdom Quote Artifact, stores specific_id, theme_ids, usage_ids)
5	  2. 'containers' (0002... : Origin / Franchise / Creator / Persona)
6	  3. 'specifics'  (0003... : Specific Endpoint / Work / Character / Diary / Wisdom / Thought on)
7	                    Holds default_usage_ids to auto-select usage options.
8	  4. 'themes'     (0004... : Sovereign Hierarchical Tree with child_of parent link)
9	  5. 'usages'     (0005... : Niche Usage Modes with Conflict Matrix)
10	Zero sentiment field, zero redundant shadow tables, zero duplicate timestamps.
11	"""
12	
13	import sqlite3
14	import json
15	import os
16	from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
17	
18	BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
19	DEFAULT_DB_PATH = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "data", "rose_quotes.db")
20	
21	
22	def get_connection(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> sqlite3.Connection:
23	    """Creates a connection configured with WAL and concurrency pragmas."""
24	    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path)), exist_ok=True)
25	    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0)
26	    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
27	    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;")
28	    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;")
29	    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;")
30	    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
31	    return conn
32	
33	
34	def init_db(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> None:
35	    """Initializes the pure 5-table relational schema."""
36	    conn = get_connection(db_path)
37	    with conn:
38	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
39	
40	        # Table 2: containers (0002...)
41	        conn.execute("""
42	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS containers (
43	                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
44	                name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
45	                type TEXT,
46	                notes TEXT
47	            );
48	        """)
49	        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_containers_name ON containers(name);")
50	
51	        # Table 3: specifics (0003...) with date & default_usage_ids
52	        conn.execute("""
53	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS specifics (
54	                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
55	                name TEXT NOT NULL,
56	                container_id TEXT NOT NULL,
57	                category TEXT,
58	                date TEXT,
59	                default_usage_ids TEXT,
60	                notes TEXT,
61	                FOREIGN KEY (container_id) REFERENCES containers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
62	            );
63	        """)
64	        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_container ON specifics(container_id);")
65	        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_name ON specifics(name);")
66	
67	        s_cols = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(specifics);").fetchall()]
68	        if s_cols:
69	            if "default_usage_ids" not in s_cols:
70	                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE specifics ADD COLUMN default_usage_ids TEXT;")
71	            if "date" not in s_cols:
72	                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE specifics ADD COLUMN date TEXT;")
73	        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_date ON specifics(date);")
74	
75	        # Table 4: themes (0004... with child_of tree relation)
76	        conn.execute("""
77	            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS themes (
78	                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
79	                name TEXT NOT NULL,
80	                child_of TEXT,
81	                notes TEXT,
82	                FOREIGN KEY (child_of) REFERENCES themes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
83	            );
84	        """)
85	        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_themes_child_of ON themes(child_of);")

467	    init_db(db_path)

469	    with conn:
470	        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
471	
472	        sid = quote.get("specific_id")
473	        if not sid and quote.get("specific_ids"):
474	            sids = quote["specific_ids"]
475	            sid = sids[0] if isinstance(sids, list) and sids else str(sids)
476	
477	        raw_themes = quote.get("theme_ids", [])
478	        theme_ids_json = json.dumps(raw_themes if isinstance(raw_themes, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)
479	
480	        raw_usage = quote.get("usage_ids", quote.get("usage", []))
481	        usage_json = json.dumps(raw_usage if isinstance(raw_usage, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)
482	
483	        preference = quote.get("preference", [])
484	        preference_json_str = json.dumps(preference if isinstance(preference, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)
485	
486	        backlinks = quote.get("backlink", quote.get("backlinks", []))
487	        backlinks_json_str = json.dumps(backlinks if isinstance(backlinks, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)
488	
489	        # Process scores (list of numbers e.g. [5, 6, 4, 7, 5])
490	        raw_scores = quote.get("scores")
491	        if raw_scores is None:
492	            raw_scores = quote.get("score_list")
493	
494	        clean_scores = None
495	        if raw_scores is not None:
496	            if isinstance(raw_scores, str):
497	                try:
498	                    parsed = json.loads(raw_scores)
499	                    if isinstance(parsed, list):
500	                        raw_scores = parsed
501	                    else:
502	                        raw_scores = [parsed]
503	                except Exception:
504	                    clean_str = raw_scores.strip().strip("[]")
505	                    raw_scores = [x.strip() for x in clean_str.split(",") if x.strip()]
506	
507	            clean_scores = []
508	            if isinstance(raw_scores, list):
509	                for s in raw_scores:
510	                    try:
511	                        num = float(s)
512	                        clean_scores.append(int(num) if num.is_integer() else round(num, 2))
513	                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
514	                        pass
515	
516	        # If scores was omitted in partial update, retain existing scores from DB
517	        if clean_scores is None:
518	            existing_record = get_quote(quote["id"], db_path)
519	            if existing_record and existing_record.get("scores") is not None:
520	                clean_scores = existing_record.get("scores", [])
521	            else:
522	                clean_scores = []
523	
524	        scores_json = json.dumps(clean_scores, ensure_ascii=False)
525	
526	        # Average score (numeric mean e.g. 5.4)
527	        avg_score = quote.get("average_score")
528	        if avg_score is None:
529	            avg_score = quote.get("avg_score")
530	
531	        if avg_score is not None and avg_score != "":
532	            try:
533	                avg_score = round(float(avg_score), 2)
534	            except (ValueError, TypeError):
535	                avg_score = None
536	        else:
537	            avg_score = None
538	
539	        # Auto-compute average if scores is present and avg_score was not explicitly specified
540	        if avg_score is None and clean_scores:
541	            calculated = sum(clean_scores) / len(clean_scores)
542	            avg_score = round(calculated, 2)
543	
544	        idx = quote.get("idx") or quote.get("index")
545	        if not idx:
546	            existing = get_quote(quote["id"], db_path)
547	            if existing:
548	                idx = existing.get("idx") or existing.get("index")
549	            else:
550	                idx = get_next_index(db_path)
551	        idx = int(idx)
552	
553	        conn.execute("DELETE FROM quotes WHERE idx = ? AND id != ?;", (idx, quote["id"]))
554	
555	        conn.execute("""
556	            INSERT INTO quotes (
557	                id, idx, main_content, context, date,
558	                specific_id, theme_ids, usage_ids, preference, backlinks,
559	                scores, average_score

562	                idx = excluded.idx,
563	                main_content = excluded.main_content,
564	                context = excluded.context,
565	                date = excluded.date,
566	                specific_id = excluded.specific_id,
567	                theme_ids = excluded.theme_ids,
568	                usage_ids = excluded.usage_ids,
569	                preference = excluded.preference,
570	                backlinks = excluded.backlinks,
571	                scores = excluded.scores,
572	                average_score = excluded.average_score;
573	        """, (
574	            quote["id"],
575	            idx,
576	            quote["main_content"].strip(),
577	            quote.get("context", "").strip(),
578	            str(quote["date"]).strip(),
579	            sid,

581	            usage_json,
582	            preference_json_str,
583	            backlinks_json_str,
584	            scores_json,
585	            avg_score
586	        ))
587	    conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);")
588	    conn.close()
589	
590	    if compile_after:
591	        try:
592	            from compile_projections import compile_projections

"""
Entropy Rose / Prescripts: Pure 5-Tier Relational SQLite Engine.
Establishes the definitive schema:
  1. 'quotes'     (0001... : Wisdom Quote Artifact, stores specific_id, theme_ids, usage_ids)
  2. 'containers' (0002... : Origin / Franchise / Creator / Persona)
  3. 'specifics'  (0003... : Specific Endpoint / Work / Character / Diary / Wisdom / Thought on)
                    Holds default_usage_ids to auto-select usage options.
  4. 'themes'     (0004... : Sovereign Hierarchical Tree with child_of parent link)
  5. 'usages'     (0005... : Niche Usage Modes with Conflict Matrix)
Zero sentiment field, zero redundant shadow tables, zero duplicate timestamps.
"""

import sqlite3
import json
import os
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional

BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "data", "rose_quotes.db")


def get_connection(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> sqlite3.Connection:
    """Creates a connection configured with WAL and concurrency pragmas."""
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(db_path)), exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path, timeout=5.0)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
    conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;")
    conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;")
    return conn


def init_db(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> None:
    """Initializes the pure 5-table relational schema."""
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")

        # Table 2: containers (0002...)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS containers (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
                type TEXT,
                notes TEXT
            );
        """)
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_containers_name ON containers(name);")

        # Table 3: specifics (0003...) with date & default_usage_ids
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS specifics (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                container_id TEXT NOT NULL,
                category TEXT,
                date TEXT,
                default_usage_ids TEXT,
                notes TEXT,
                FOREIGN KEY (container_id) REFERENCES containers(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
            );
        """)
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_container ON specifics(container_id);")
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_name ON specifics(name);")

        s_cols = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(specifics);").fetchall()]
        if s_cols:
            if "default_usage_ids" not in s_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE specifics ADD COLUMN default_usage_ids TEXT;")
            if "date" not in s_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE specifics ADD COLUMN date TEXT;")
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_specifics_date ON specifics(date);")

        # Table 4: themes (0004... with child_of tree relation)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS themes (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                child_of TEXT,
                notes TEXT,
                FOREIGN KEY (child_of) REFERENCES themes(id) ON DELETE SET NULL
            );
        """)
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_themes_child_of ON themes(child_of);")
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_themes_name ON themes(name);")

        # Table 5: usages (0005... with conflict matrix)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS usages (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                name TEXT NOT NULL,
                description TEXT,
                icon TEXT,
                conflicts_with TEXT
            );
        """)

        # Table 1: quotes (0001... — zero sentiment field)
        conn.execute("""
            CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS quotes (
                id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
                idx INTEGER UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                main_content TEXT NOT NULL,
                context TEXT,
                date TEXT NOT NULL,
                specific_id TEXT,
                theme_ids TEXT,
                usage_ids TEXT,
                preference TEXT,
                backlinks TEXT,
                scores TEXT,
                average_score REAL
            );
        """)
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_quotes_idx ON quotes(idx);")
        conn.execute("CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_quotes_date ON quotes(date);")

        q_cols = [r["name"] for r in conn.execute("PRAGMA table_info(quotes);").fetchall()]
        if q_cols:
            if "theme_ids" not in q_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE quotes ADD COLUMN theme_ids TEXT;")
            if "usage_ids" not in q_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE quotes ADD COLUMN usage_ids TEXT;")
            if "specific_id" not in q_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE quotes ADD COLUMN specific_id TEXT;")
            if "scores" not in q_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE quotes ADD COLUMN scores TEXT DEFAULT '[]';")
            if "average_score" not in q_cols:
                conn.execute("ALTER TABLE quotes ADD COLUMN average_score REAL;")

    conn.close()

# TABLE 2: CONTAINERS (0002...) — CRUD
# ==============================================================================

def upsert_container(container: Dict[str, Any], db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> None:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
        name = container["name"].strip()
        cid = container["id"]
        c_type = container.get("type", "")
        notes = container.get("notes", "")
        conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO containers (id, name, type, notes)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                name = excluded.name,
                type = excluded.type,
                notes = excluded.notes;
        """, (cid, name, c_type, notes))
    conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);")
    conn.close()


def get_container(container_id: str, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("SELECT id, name, type, notes FROM containers WHERE id = ?;", (container_id,))
    row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    if not row:
        return None
    return {"id": row["id"], "name": row["name"], "type": row["type"] or "", "notes": row["notes"] or ""}


def get_all_containers(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("SELECT id, name, type, notes FROM containers ORDER BY name ASC;")
    rows = cur.fetchall()
    conn.close()
    return [{"id": r["id"], "name": r["name"], "type": r["type"] or "", "notes": r["notes"] or ""} for r in rows]


def delete_container(container_id: str, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> bool:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM containers WHERE id = ?;", (container_id,))
    conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);")
    conn.close()
    try:
        from compile_projections import compile_projections
        compile_projections(db_path)
    except Exception:
        pass
    return True

def upsert_specific(specific: Dict[str, Any], db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> None:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")
        name = specific["name"].strip()
        cid = specific["container_id"]
        date_str = str(specific.get("date", "")).strip() if specific.get("date") else ""
        usage_ids = specific.get("default_usage_ids", [])
        usage_json = json.dumps(usage_ids if isinstance(usage_ids, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)
        sid = specific["id"]
        category = specific.get("category", "")
        notes = specific.get("notes", "")

        conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO specifics (id, name, container_id, category, date, default_usage_ids, notes)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                name = excluded.name,
                container_id = excluded.container_id,
                category = excluded.category,
                date = excluded.date,
                default_usage_ids = excluded.default_usage_ids,
                notes = excluded.notes;
        """, (sid, name, cid, category, date_str, usage_json, notes))
    conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);")
    conn.close()


def get_specific(specific_id: str, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("""
        SELECT s.id, s.name, s.container_id, s.category, s.date, s.default_usage_ids, s.notes,
               c.name as container_name, c.type as container_type
        FROM specifics s
        JOIN containers c ON s.container_id = c.id
        WHERE s.id = ?;
    """, (specific_id,))
    row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    if not row:
        return None
    usages = json.loads(row["default_usage_ids"]) if row["default_usage_ids"] else []
    return {
        "id": row["id"],
        "name": row["name"],
        "container_id": row["container_id"],
        "container_name": row["container_name"],
        "container_type": row["container_type"] or "",
        "category": row["category"] or "",
        "date": row["date"] or "",
        "default_usage_ids": usages,
        "notes": row["notes"] or ""
    }


def get_all_specifics(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("""
        SELECT s.id, s.name, s.container_id, s.category, s.date, s.default_usage_ids, s.notes,
               c.name as container_name, c.type as container_type
        FROM specifics s
        JOIN containers c ON s.container_id = c.id
        ORDER BY s.name ASC;
    """)
    rows = cur.fetchall()
    conn.close()
    results = []
    for r in rows:
        usages = json.loads(r["default_usage_ids"]) if r["default_usage_ids"] else []
        results.append({
            "id": r["id"],

            "container_id": r["container_id"],
            "container_name": r["container_name"],
            "container_type": r["container_type"] or "",
            "category": r["category"] or "",
            "date": r["date"] or "",
            "default_usage_ids": usages,
            "notes": r["notes"] or ""
        })
    return results

def upsert_theme(theme: Dict[str, Any], db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> None:

        conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO themes (id, name, child_of, notes)
            VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                name = excluded.name,

def get_theme(theme_id: str, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:

def get_next_index(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> int:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(idx), 0) + 1 AS next_idx FROM quotes;")
    row = cur.fetchone()
    conn.close()
    return row["next_idx"] if row else 1


def upsert_quote(quote: Dict[str, Any], db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH, compile_after: bool = True) -> None:
    init_db(db_path)
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    with conn:
        conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE;")

        sid = quote.get("specific_id")
        if not sid and quote.get("specific_ids"):
            sids = quote["specific_ids"]
            sid = sids[0] if isinstance(sids, list) and sids else str(sids)

        raw_themes = quote.get("theme_ids", [])
        theme_ids_json = json.dumps(raw_themes if isinstance(raw_themes, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)

        raw_usage = quote.get("usage_ids", quote.get("usage", []))
        usage_json = json.dumps(raw_usage if isinstance(raw_usage, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)

        preference = quote.get("preference", [])
        preference_json_str = json.dumps(preference if isinstance(preference, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)

        backlinks = quote.get("backlink", quote.get("backlinks", []))
        backlinks_json_str = json.dumps(backlinks if isinstance(backlinks, list) else [], ensure_ascii=False)

        # Process scores (list of numbers e.g. [5, 6, 4, 7, 5])
        raw_scores = quote.get("scores")
        if raw_scores is None:
            raw_scores = quote.get("score_list")

        clean_scores = None
        if raw_scores is not None:
            if isinstance(raw_scores, str):
                try:
                    parsed = json.loads(raw_scores)
                    if isinstance(parsed, list):
                        raw_scores = parsed
                    else:
                        raw_scores = [parsed]
                except Exception:
                    clean_str = raw_scores.strip().strip("[]")
                    raw_scores = [x.strip() for x in clean_str.split(",") if x.strip()]

            clean_scores = []
            if isinstance(raw_scores, list):
                for s in raw_scores:
                    try:
                        num = float(s)
                        clean_scores.append(int(num) if num.is_integer() else round(num, 2))
                    except (ValueError, TypeError):
                        pass

        # If scores was omitted in partial update, retain existing scores from DB
        if clean_scores is None:
            existing_record = get_quote(quote["id"], db_path)
            if existing_record and existing_record.get("scores") is not None:
                clean_scores = existing_record.get("scores", [])
            else:
                clean_scores = []

        scores_json = json.dumps(clean_scores, ensure_ascii=False)

        # Average score (numeric mean e.g. 5.4)
        avg_score = quote.get("average_score")
        if avg_score is None:
            avg_score = quote.get("avg_score")

        if avg_score is not None and avg_score != "":
            try:
                avg_score = round(float(avg_score), 2)
            except (ValueError, TypeError):
                avg_score = None
        else:
            avg_score = None

        # Auto-compute average if scores is present and avg_score was not explicitly specified
        if avg_score is None and clean_scores:
            calculated = sum(clean_scores) / len(clean_scores)
            avg_score = round(calculated, 2)

        idx = quote.get("idx") or quote.get("index")
        if not idx:
            existing = get_quote(quote["id"], db_path)
            if existing:
                idx = existing.get("idx") or existing.get("index")
            else:
                idx = get_next_index(db_path)
        idx = int(idx)

        conn.execute("DELETE FROM quotes WHERE idx = ? AND id != ?;", (idx, quote["id"]))

        conn.execute("""
            INSERT INTO quotes (
                id, idx, main_content, context, date,
                specific_id, theme_ids, usage_ids, preference, backlinks,
                scores, average_score
            ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
            ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET
                idx = excluded.idx,
                main_content = excluded.main_content,
                context = excluded.context,
                date = excluded.date,
                specific_id = excluded.specific_id,
                theme_ids = excluded.theme_ids,
                usage_ids = excluded.usage_ids,
                preference = excluded.preference,
                backlinks = excluded.backlinks,
                scores = excluded.scores,
                average_score = excluded.average_score;
        """, (
            quote["id"],
            idx,
            quote["main_content"].strip(),
            quote.get("context", "").strip(),
            str(quote["date"]).strip(),
            sid,
            theme_ids_json,
            usage_json,
            preference_json_str,
            backlinks_json_str,
            scores_json,
            avg_score
        ))
    conn.execute("PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);")
    conn.close()

    if compile_after:
        try:
            from compile_projections import compile_projections
            compile_projections(db_path)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[WARN] Projection compilation error: {e}")


def get_quote(quote_id: str, db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:
    conn = get_connection(db_path)
    cur = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM quotes WHERE id = ?;", (quote_id,))
    row = cur.fetchone()
    if not row:
        conn.close()
        return None

    sid = row["specific_id"]
    themes = json.loads(row["theme_ids"]) if ("theme_ids" in row.keys() and row["theme_ids"]) else []
    usage = json.loads(row["usage_ids"]) if ("usage_ids" in row.keys() and row["usage_ids"]) else []
    preference = json.loads(row["preference"]) if row["preference"] else []
    backlinks = json.loads(row["backlinks"]) if row["backlinks"] else []

"""
Entropy Rose / Prescripts: Deterministic CQRS Projection Compiler.
Compiles the pure 5-table relational schema:
  quotes -> specifics -> containers + themes (child_of tree) + usages (conflict matrix)
into O(1) denormalized JSON projection maps for Obsidian and edge clients.
Zero sentiment field, completely clean relational mappings.
"""

import sqlite3
import json
import os
from typing import Dict, Any, List

BASE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
DEFAULT_DB_PATH = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "data", "rose_quotes.db")
DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "data")


def compile_projections(db_path: str = DEFAULT_DB_PATH, out_dir: str = DEFAULT_OUT_DIR) -> Dict[str, int]:
    """
    Reads authoritative SQLite tables and generates:
      1. quotes_map.json: { [hex_id]: QuoteObject } (Denormalized with Specifics, Containers, Themes, Usages)
      2. taxonomy_index.json: { containers: [...], specifics: [...], themes: [...], usages: [...] }
    """
    if not os.path.exists(db_path):
        return {"quotes": 0, "specifics": 0, "containers": 0, "themes": 0, "usages": 0}

    os.makedirs(out_dir, exist_ok=True)
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row

    # 1. Fetch all containers (Table 2)
    containers_map = {}
    containers_list = []
    try:
        cur = conn.execute("SELECT id, name, type, notes FROM containers ORDER BY name ASC;")
        for r in cur.fetchall():
            c = {
                "id": r["id"],
                "name": r["name"],
                "type": r["type"] or "",
                "notes": r["notes"] or ""
            }
            containers_map[r["id"]] = c
            containers_list.append(c)
    except sqlite3.OperationalError:
        pass

    # 2. Fetch all usages (Table 5) with conflict matrix
    usages_map = {}
    usages_list = []
    try:
        cur = conn.execute("SELECT id, name, description, icon, COALESCE(conflicts_with, '[]') as conflicts_with FROM usages ORDER BY name ASC;")
        for r in cur.fetchall():
            conflicts = json.loads(r["conflicts_with"]) if r["conflicts_with"] else []
            u = {
                "id": r["id"],
                "name": r["name"],
                "description": r["description"] or "",
                "icon": r["icon"] or "",
                "conflicts_with": conflicts
            }
            usages_map[r["id"]] = u
            usages_list.append(u)
    except sqlite3.OperationalError:
        pass

    # 3. Fetch all specifics (Table 3) pre-joined with containers, dates and default_usage_ids
    specifics_map = {}
    specifics_list = []

input.content: # Architectural Analysis: Entropy Rose Data Engine & Universal Table Builder Blueprint > **Target**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\RAM\README.md` > **Source Engine Analyzed**: `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Entropy\Rose` > **Authority**: The Manager | **Analysis & Blueprint**: Faust > **Purpose**: Deconstruct how Entropy Rose handles relational and tabular data, catalog every data entry modality, and establish the engineering blueprint for a custom Notion-like Table Designer UI. --- ## Executive Summary **Entropy Rose** (`Prescripts Studio`) is a deterministic, lightweight, pure 5-tier relational database system with an integrated single-page management studio. It was engineered to solve a common software defect: *schema rot and UI lock-in*. Instead of writing rigid, hardcoded forms for each table, Rose employs a **Declarative Meta-Configuration Architecture** (`TABLES_CONFIG`) paired with **Dual-State CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)**: 1. **Authoritative Write Core (OLTP)**: Pure SQLite in WAL mode enforcing relational integrity, foreign keys, and indexes. 2. **Instant Read Projections (OLAP)**: Zero-latency compiled JSON maps (`quotes_map.json`, `taxonomy_index.json`) for $O(1)$ consumer access and edge microcontrollers (ESP32 via Turso cloud sync). 3. **Soft-Coded Studio UI**: A single declarative JavaScript dictionary renders interactive tables, filter bars, searchers, and CRUD modal dialogs on the fly for any registered entity. This architecture serves as the direct operational foundation for building a **Universal Custom Table Builder** (a sovereign Notion-like database designer). --- ## Part 1: How Entropy Rose Handles Its Data ### 1.1 The Pure 5-Tier Relational Schema Rose rejects flat, unindexed JSON dumps and messy shadow tables in favor of a normalized 5-table relational layout in SQLite: ``` ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TABLE 2: containers │ │ [id: 0002...] (Origin, Franchise, Creator, Persona: e.g. William Blake, Evangelion) │ └──────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ 1:N (Foreign Key: container_id) ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TABLE 3: specifics │ │ [id: 0003...] (Specific Endpoint: Work, Character, Chapter, Diary Entry, Principle) │ │ Holds default_usage_ids (JSON) to auto-select operational modes on citation │ └──────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │ 1:N (Foreign Key: specific_id) ▼ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ TABLE 1: quotes │ │ [id: 0001...] (Wisdom Artifact: main_content, context, flexible date, sequence idx) │ │ - specific_id -> FK to Table 3 │ │ - theme_ids -> JSON Array referencing Table 4 │ │ - usage_ids -> JSON Array referencing Table 5 │ │ - preference -> JSON Array referencing Table 1 (Self-Referential Response Quotes) │ │ - backlinks -> JSON Array of URIs / URLs (Obsidian / Web) │ │ - scores -> JSON Array of numbers [5, 6, 4, 7, 5] │ │ - average_score -> REAL / Float (Computed arithmetic mean e.g. 5.4) │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ▲ ▲ │ N:M (Foreign Key Array) │ N:M (Foreign Key Array) ┌───────────────────┴────────────────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐ │ TABLE 4: themes │ │ TABLE 5: usages │ │ [id: 0004...] │ │ [id: 0005...] │ │ Hierarchical Tree via self-referential │ │ Operational Modes (Rewrite Craft, │ │ child_of FK -> themes.id │ │ Diary Prompt, Daily Rule) with │ │ │ │ conflicts_with JSON Array matrix │ └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ### 1.2 Deterministic 16-Character Hex Identifiers Rose enforces a deterministic, human-inspectable primary key format: $$\text{ID} = \langle\text{4-Hex Table Prefix}\rangle + \langle\text{12-Hex Unix Milliseconds}\rangle$$ - `0001...`: **Quotes** (Table 1) - `0002...`: **Containers** (Table 2) - `0003...`: **Specifics** (Table 3) - `0004...`: **Themes** (Table 4) - `0005...`: **Usages** (Table 5) - Example: `00010001A1088D80` - **Architectural Advantage**: 1. **$O(1)$ Chronological Sorting**: Simply ordering by `id ASC/DESC` naturally sorts records by creation time without requiring a redundant `created_at` timestamp column. 2. **Domain Isolation**: Any string in the system immediately reveals what entity type it belongs to just by reading the first 4 characters. 3. **Universal Foreign Keys**: Foreign relations are pure 16-character strings, preventing type confusion. --- ### 1.3 Concurrency & SQLite Persistence Invariants (`db.py`) Rose configures SQLite with high-reliability enterprise pragmas: ```python conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;") # Concurrent reads while writing conn.execute("PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;") # Maximum performance without corruption risk conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000;") # 5-second lock queue before timeout conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;") # Strict relational integrity enforcement ``` Every mutation runs inside an explicit `BEGIN IMMEDIATE;` transaction and triggers a passive checkpoint `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(PASSIVE);` upon commit. --- ### 1.4 CQRS Dual-State Projection Engine (`compile_projections.py`) To prevent expensive multi-table `JOIN` operations whenever an edge device (like an ESP32 or Obsidian plugin) requests data, Rose uses **CQRS Compilation**: 1. When a record is created, edited, or deleted in SQLite, `compile_projections(db_path)` is automatically triggered. 2. It compiles the authoritative relational tables into two denormalized, read-optimized JSON artifacts: - `quotes_map.json`: A dictionary `{[hex_id]: FullDenormalizedQuote}` with resolved container names, endpoint details, and theme names. - `taxonomy_index.json`: Flat lists of containers, specifics, themes, and usages for instant dropdown auto-completion. 3. This guarantees that read performance is always $O(1)$ memory lookup, while write performance retains full ACID transactional safety. --- ### 1.5 Edge Distribution & Cloud Sync (`turso_sync.py`) Rose integrates a one-way cloud synchronization pipeline to **Turso Cloud (libSQL)**: - Local SQLite is always the authoritative master. - When the Manager triggers "Save to Turso" (from the Studio header button or CLI), the local state is cleanly dumped and synchronized to the cloud instance, allowing remote ESP32 hardware displays to fetch morning quotes over HTTPS without opening local ports. --- ## Part 2: Comprehensive Catalog of Data Entry Types in Rose Entropy Rose implements **15 distinct data entry modalities and field types**. Each type is tailored for a specific relational or cognitive requirement: | # | Field Type Slug | UI Component / Widget | SQLite Storage Type | In-Memory Format | Notion / Database Equivalent | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **1** | `readonly` | Disabled monospaced text box | `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` | String (`"0001..."`) | Auto-generated ID (`ID`) | | **2** | `text` | Single-line `` | `TEXT` | String | Single-line Text (`Text`) | | **3** | `textarea` | Resizable `

# Strategic Briefing: Entropy Rose Data Architecture & Universal Table Builder Blueprint

Manager, I have completed a thorough deconstruction of `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\Entropy\Rose` and documented the entire system breakdown along with the engineering blueprint for your custom Notion-like Table Designer UI in `D:\My Drive\Blue AI\RAM\README.md`.

---

## 1. How Entropy Rose Handles Its Data

Entropy Rose uses a **Declarative Meta-Configuration Architecture** backed by a **Dual-State CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)** pattern:

1. **Authoritative Relational Core (SQLite in WAL Mode)**:
   - Configured with `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL;`, `synchronous = NORMAL;`, and `foreign_keys = ON;`.
   - Organizes data into 5 normalized relational tiers (`quotes`, `containers`, `specifics`, `themes`, `usages`).
   - Every mutation runs in an explicit transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE;`) and automatically triggers a passive WAL checkpoint.
2. **Deterministic 16-Character Hex Identifiers**:
   - Primary Keys follow `<4-HEX-PREFIX><12-HEX-UNIX-MS>` (e.g. `00010001A1088D80`).
   - Provides native **$O(1)$ chronological sorting** without redundant timestamp columns and ensures instant domain recognition (`0001` = Quote, `0002` = Container, `0003` = Specific, `0004` = Theme, `0005` = Usage).
3. **CQRS Compiled Projections (`compile_projections.py`)**:
   - Compiles relational tables into denormalized read-optimized JSON artifacts (`quotes_map.json` and `taxonomy_index.json`).
   - Consumer reads (web UI, Obsidian second-brain integrations, ESP32 edge displays) achieve instant $O(1)$ lookup performance with zero runtime multi-table `JOIN` overhead.
4. **Edge Cloud Sync (`turso_sync.py`)**:
   - Provides a one-way replication pipeline from local master SQLite to Turso Cloud (libSQL) to power remote ESP32 hardware without exposing local ports.

---

## 2. Complete Inventory: 15 Data Entry Modalities in Rose

Rose implements **15 distinct data entry types and interaction widgets** across its Studio UI:

| # | Data Entry Type | UI Component / Widget | SQLite Storage Format | Notion Equivalent | Key Behavioral Characteristics |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | `readonly` | Monospaced disabled text box | `TEXT PRIMARY KEY` | Auto-generated ID (`ID`) | Deterministic hex generation (`generateHexId`), non-editable. |
| **2** | `text` | Single-line `<input type="text">` | `TEXT` | Single-line Text (`Text`) | Basic string input with auto-trim and amber focus glow. |
| **3** | `textarea` | Resizable `<textarea>` (JetBrains Mono) | `TEXT` | Long-form Text / Notes (`Text`) | Preserves stanzas, line breaks, and raw indentations verbatim. |
| **4** | `number` | Numeric `<input type="number">` | `INTEGER` | Number (`Number` - Integer) | Monotonic integer sequences (`MAX(idx) + 1` auto-increment). |
| **5** | `decimal_number` | Number input with `step="0.1"` | `REAL` | Number (`Number` - Decimal) | Floating point ratings and ratios rounded to 2 decimal places. |
| **6** | `scores_array` | Array input with auto-mean hook | `TEXT` (JSON Array) | Formula / Rollup Rating | Parses `[5, 6, 4]`, live-calculates arithmetic mean on every keystroke. |
| **7** | `date` (Flexible) | Input with Dropdown Suggestor | `TEXT` | Date (`Date` with flexible precision) | Accepts years (`2020`), months (`2023-05`), full dates, or ranges (`2020~2023-05`). |
| **8** | `select` | Notion Combobox with Search & Create | `TEXT` (Foreign Key) | Relation (`Relation` - 1:1 / 1:N) | Searchable dropdown with inline `+ Create new record` shortcut. |
| **9** | `select` (Tree) | Indented Tree Select (`child_of`) | `TEXT` (Self-referential FK) | Parent / Sub-item Hierarchy | Visual indentation (`📁 Root` vs `↳ 🏷️ Child`); prevents self-selection loops. |
| **10** | `multi_select` | Searchable Badge / Chip Array | `TEXT` (JSON Array) | Multi-select (`Multi-select`) | Interactive chips with individual remove buttons (`✕`) and filter box. |
| **11** | `conflict_matrix` | Mutually Exclusive Checkbox Pills | `TEXT` (JSON Array) | Constraint-Enforced Multi-Select | Auto-deselects conflicting modes based on `conflicts_with` matrix. |
| **12** | `preference` | Inter-Record Entity Linker | `TEXT` (JSON Array) | Self-Referential Relation / Backlink | Searches other records in the same table; renders preview, stores ID. |
| **13** | `json_array` | Comma-delimited String/URL list | `TEXT` (JSON Array) | URL / Deep-Link Reference | Parses web links (`🔗 hostname.com`) and Obsidian URIs (`obsidian://...`). |
| **14** | `table_column` | Formatted Column Cell | N/A (View Grid) | Table Column Formatter | Renders badges, monospaced tags, and bold text based on schema formatters. |
| **15** | `live_json` | Sticky Real-Time JSON Code Mirror | N/A (Inspector) | State Inspector | Live reactive mirror displaying exact payload before committing to SQLite. |

---

## 3. How the Soft-Coded Studio UI Works

In `prescripts_entry.html`, tables are **not hardcoded**. They are driven by a single JavaScript dictionary: `TABLES_CONFIG`:
- **`columns` Array**: Controls grid display headers, styling (`isMono`, `isBold`), and custom cell render formatters (`format: (val, row) => ...`).
- **`fields` Array**: Controls the modal editor. A generic loop inspects each field's `type` and dynamically injects the appropriate input widget (text, textarea, select, multi-select, scores array).
- **CRUD Endpoints**: Generic hooks (`saveEndpoint`, `deleteEndpoint`, `getData()`) route operations uniformly.

---

## 4. Blueprint for Your Custom Notion-Like Table Designer App

To turn this into an app that lets you design arbitrary Notion-like databases from scratch, we elevate Rose’s pattern to a **Meta-Schema Engine**:

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                             TIER 1: THE META-SCHEMA                              │
│  Tables storing table and property definitions                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  1. `meta_tables`  : id, slug, name, icon, description, created_at, updated_at   │
│  2. `meta_columns` : id, table_id, key, name, property_type, config_json, ord    │
└────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │ Governs
                                         ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     TIER 2: HYBRID DOCUMENT STORAGE (SQLITE)                     │
│  Universal records table with SQLite JSON1 indexing                             │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  `custom_records`: id, table_id, idx, title, data (JSON), created_at, updated_at │
└────────────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                         │ Powers
                                         ▼
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                         TIER 3: THE UI STUDIO INTERFACE                          │
│  1. Schema Designer: Add/reorder columns, select property type, set colors/options│
│  2. Data Grid View : Dynamic Notion table view with sorting and instant search   │
│  3. Modal Inspector: Auto-rendered edit form adhering to Rose's 15 input widgets  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### Architectural Recommendations:
1. **Hybrid Document Storage**: Rather than running risky `CREATE TABLE` and `ALTER TABLE` DDL queries every time you add a column, store custom records in a universal `custom_records` table with a `data` JSON column indexed by SQLite JSON1 (`json_extract(data, '$.status')`).
2. **Master UI/UX Alignment**: Apply the **Zero-Dead-Zone Delegation** pattern from `.claude/templates/ui/`, ensuring 100% Fitts's Law hitboxes for all dropdown options and pills, and soft-coded theme tokens (`data-theme="dark"` / `data-theme="light"`).
3. **Storage Invariant**: Keep all databases and assets on **Local Disk `D:\`**.

The full, in-depth architectural specification and implementation guide is written and available at:
`D:\My Drive\Blue AI\RAM\README.md`
